review_notes: I read the whole file and the YoungSubgroup, Partitions and RowColumnSubgroup declarations it builds on. I searched Mathlib's Combinatorics/Young for a sigma-type or cell-equivalence API and found none. The private `rowBlocks` and `rowCellsEquiv` are file-local bridges between `YoungDiagram.cells` and the same sigma shape that `youngBlocksEquiv` already uses. They don't compete with a Mathlib concept. `youngSubgroupConjMulEquiv` is built from Mathlib's `MulAut.conj`, `MulEquiv.subgroupMap` and `MulEquiv.subgroupCongr`, so it is a named specialisation and not a rival definition. `rowYoungConjugator` is a specific permutation built from `Equiv.trans` and `Equiv.cast`, with no Mathlib counterpart. I found no avoidable duplicate of a Mathlib concept. The only uncertainty is that I did not search all of Mathlib for an equivalent of the Young-diagram row/cell sigma decomposition.
